stemMd: The author mentions that "The inspectors, meanwhile, kept their jobs" mainly in order to

options.label: A
options.textMd: explain why the system raised so many alerts in its first year.

options.label: B
options.textMd: show that monitoring supports inspection rather than replacing it.

options.label: C
options.textMd: suggest that the whole monitoring project had wasted the authority's money.

options.label: D
options.textMd: criticise the authority for keeping staff it no longer needed.

options.label: E
options.textMd: show that the inspectors had designed the improved alert system.

explanationMd:
To find the purpose of a sentence, read the sentence that follows it: it often gives the reason. Here it does: "A sensor can report that something has changed; someone still has to go and see what it is." The sensors detect a change; a person is still needed to find out what the change is. So the inspectors kept their jobs because monitoring and inspection do different things, and the passage presents them as working together.

This also closes the circle opened in the first paragraph, where looking was described as the old method with obvious limits. The ending makes clear that the new method fills those gaps without making the old one unnecessary. Check the other readings: the passage reports that the alerts became "worth reading", so it does not present the project as a waste, and it gives the inspectors a continuing task, so it does not call them unneeded.

distractorRationale.c: By the end the alerts had fallen to a handful a year, "each one ... now worth reading". The passage presents the project as working, and keeping the inspectors is explained, not criticised.
distractorRationale.a: The first-year alerts are explained in the third paragraph, by weather and traffic. The sentence about the inspectors comes after the problem has been solved and is about a different point.
distractorRationale.e: The improved alerts were built by "the team" from a record of readings. The passage never says the inspectors designed them.
distractorRationale.d: The very next sentence says that someone still has to go and see what a change is, which is the inspectors' work. They are presented as still needed, not as surplus staff.

accessibilityText: A purpose question about the bridge monitoring passage. It asks why the author mentions that "The inspectors, meanwhile, kept their jobs". The five choices: explain why the system raised so many alerts in its first year; show that monitoring supports inspection rather than replacing it; suggest that the whole monitoring project had wasted the authority's money; criticise the authority for keeping staff it no longer needed; show that the inspectors had designed the improved alert system.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage; it tests the function of a sentence within the conclusion of a passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-i-wave8-verbal-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The next sentence explains it: a sensor reports that something has changed, but someone must still go and see what it is, so monitoring supports inspection rather than replacing it. The remark does not explain the first-year alerts or call the project wasted (the alerts became 'worth reading'). It does not criticise keeping staff, and the passage never says the inspectors designed the new alert system. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolci-verbal-run1) reached the same answer: The next sentence explains: a sensor reports a change but someone must go and see what it is, so monitoring supports rather than replaces inspection. Nothing suggests wasted money, criticism of keeping staff, inspectors designing the system, or a link to first-year alerts.]
